headlines.title: Afghanistan says 28 fighters killed after crossing from Pakistan; Islamabad denies ties - Reuters
Pakistan Finance Minister's US Exim talks covered financing for Boeing aircraft, adviser says - Reuters
UP man held in Pakistan spying case freed after 22 years
Info ministry rejects Afghan Taliban's 'frivolous' claims linking Pakistan to reported Nuristan violence
Deported from Pakistan, Sanaullah left his business behind

brief.text:
SITUATION NOW
Afghanistan reported that 28 fighters were killed after crossing from Pakistan, but Islamabad denies ties. [1]
Pakistan's Finance Minister discussed financing for Boeing aircraft during US Exim talks, according to an adviser. [2]

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR PAKISTAN
The US Exim talks on Boeing financing occur while Pakistan is linked to 169 US OFAC and Canada SEMA sanctions designations. [2][E3]

KEY RISKS
The most severe government travel advisory for Pakistan is Reconsider Travel, reflecting risks for foreign nationals. [E2]

OUTLOOK
A Polymarket market on Pakistan military action against Yemen by October 31, 2026 is priced Yes at 8% as of Sep 28, 2026. [E5]
A Polymarket market on whether India will strike Pakistan by December 31, 2026 is priced Yes at 13% as of Sep 28, 2026. [E6]

WATCH ITEMS
The outcome of the US Exim talks on financing for Boeing aircraft remains unresolved. [2]
It is unresolved whether Pakistan will take military action against Yemen by October 31, 2026. [E5]
